summary: The finite minimax theorem, exact state-aware repair, source-relative hclose chain, and successor-program identities are mathematically sound at their stated scope. The general finite-horizon sufficient-state proposition needs explicit matched-input, initial-history, and common-kernel hypotheses; asymptotic uniformity and two ancillary descriptions also need small clarifications.

details.review_scope: One bounded fresh mathematical pre-submission audit; no manuscript edits, external model calls, new experiments, publication action, project-state read, prior-audit read, or automatic next round.

acceptance_gate.note: PA-01 and PA-02 prevent a clean PASS; no FATAL or CRITICAL issue was found.

issues.statement: Equal initial compact states imply the same finite-horizon joint law under the three listed conditions.
issues.note: The induction also needs a matched exogenous-input mechanism, equal initial policy-visible history or policy factorisation through the compact state, and common measurable joint kernels.
issues.counterexample: YES: equal constant compact states with different future inputs and observation equal to input; independently, equal compact states with different visible initial histories and a policy that chooses the last visible bit.
issues.minimal_fix: Declare a common measurable exogenous-input kernel and common joint action, observation-cost, and compact-state update kernels; assume equal initial policy-visible histories or require all history dependence to factor through the compact record; condition the induction on the full shared finite history.

issues.statement: Several local residuals have the displayed big-O orders.
issues.note: The coefficients and orders are correct, but the text should state tau tends to zero with fixed a,b and fixed functions/cutoffs and no claimed uniformity over those data.
issues.counterexample: NO under the intended fixed-data reading.
issues.minimal_fix: Add one sentence declaring tau -> 0, fixed a,b and fixed coefficient functions/cutoffs, implied-constant dependence on those data, and no wider uniformity.

issues.statement: A compatible basis rescaling leaves the represented action unchanged.
issues.note: The displayed algebra proves r'=r and H'y'=Hy, but the corresponding amplitude transformation and represented action are not defined.
issues.counterexample: CANDIDATE outside the intended condition: rescale the basis without inverse amplitude rescaling.
issues.minimal_fix: Define a_i'=a_i/lambda_i for b_i'=lambda_i b_i and show a_i'b_i'=a_i b_i, while stating lambda_i positivity and the source multiplier bounds.

issues.statement: The deterministic HClose harness checks the scalar closure cases.
issues.note: positive_case is computed but never asserted or returned. The universal inequality is correctly supplied by the written proof, so this is not a semantic gap.
issues.minimal_fix: Assert sp.simplify(positive_case) == 0 or remove the unused variable and describe the narrower symbolic coverage.

claim_boundaries_preserved: The finite witness compares equal readout r, not equal targets, complete states, or full functions.
The readout-only lower bound is for deterministic scalar g depending only on r.
The exact repair is local to the inner rectangle and does not prove global PDE admissibility or norm improvement.
The hclose result is an application of supplied source lemmas and a supplied downstream consumer, not a new global Navier-Stokes theorem.
Stored compiler acceptance is not upgraded to a fresh kernel certification.
Successor traces show particular revision and reuse but no stable average causal benefit.
